title: Joining Sidney Desvigne on the Streckfus boats
summary: Eugene Ware recommended him to Desvigne; after a year of waiting he joined the orchestra on the Streckfus line and the Idlewild.

venues.name: Streckfus steamer City of New Orleans

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: And when I was playing with Kit Harris, a fellow by the name of Eugene Ware, he was a trumpet player in the Desvene's orchestra. And he came up there to hear us one night rehearsal and Desvene at that particular time he needed a trombone player. And Mr. Ware must have went and told Desvene that if you want a good trombone player you can get him one. So after I lost my wife, I waited a year and I happened to go by the Bulls, you know where that is. Bulls uptown. And this fellow Ware saw me and he called me. And Sidney asked me was I doing anything and I told him no. So he said be out on the, I forget the name of that boat, no it wasn't the captain. Sidney New Orleans, be out there for rehearsal. So I went out there that Tuesday and I made rehearsal and then I got with Sidney Desvene's orchestra. I played with him for a number of years. What line was it?
That's the Streckfus line. The Streckfus line. And after they discarded the city of New Orleans then the capital took its place.
You don't remember the city of New Orleans.

You don't. Then they had another boat we used to have, it was a colored excursion boat, it used to be at the foot of Napoleon Avenue called Idlewild. We played on that for a couple of weeks. And then we went up the river. Was that just for colored then? Just for colored, that boat up at Napoleon Avenue, yes. And then we went, used to go up the river as far as St. Paul, Minnesota every year for about five or six years.
